# How to Fix Bambu Studio Non-Manifold Edges Error (2026 Slicer Guide)

:::ai-answer
In Bambu Studio, 'non-manifold edges' means edges shared by one or three-plus faces instead of exactly two, so the slicer cannot tell inside from outside.
:::

You imported a model into **Bambu Studio** and a warning icon appeared next to it, with a message such as *"Error: 12 non-manifold edges"*. This guide explains what the message means, when a single edge is safe to ignore, why Fix Model is missing on macOS and Linux, what to do when the repair crashes, and how to repair the file outside the slicer.

---

## What Does "Non-Manifold Edges" Mean in Bambu Studio?

In computational geometry, a **manifold 3D mesh** is "watertight": it divides space into an unambiguous inside and outside, and every edge is shared by **exactly two faces**.

A **[non-manifold edge](/glossary/non-manifold-edges)** breaks that rule:

1. **Boundary Edges (Holes in the Mesh):** An edge is connected to only *one* polygon. The mesh has an open seam, so the model is a thin shell rather than a solid.
2. **T-Junctions (3+ Polygons Sharing an Edge):** An internal rib or intersecting wall shares an edge with the outer surface. The slicer cannot tell which side is plastic and which is air.
3. **Non-Manifold Vertices (Hourglass Cones):** Two volumes touch at a single point without sharing a connecting volume.

When the slicer cuts such a mesh into layers, it cannot always close each layer's outline, which shows up as gaps in walls, missing layers or infill where there should be none.

:::callout
💡 **Quick check:** run the **[free STL check](/tools/repair-stl-online)** to see the count of open holes, non-manifold edges and flipped normals before you slice — nothing to install.
:::

---

## Bambu Studio non-manifold edge error — the exact message and what triggers it

Bambu Studio puts a warning icon next to the object with a tooltip such as **Error: 12 non-manifold edges, 3 non-manifold vertices** (or **Error: 1 non-manifold edge**) and the hint *Right click the icon to fix model object*; plain holes appear as **Info: 4 open edges**. It shows up when the mesh it loads has edges that are not shared by exactly two triangles — usually holes, internal walls or overlapping shells left by the export, a boolean or the cut tool.

These are Bambu Studio's own message strings ([message catalogue on GitHub](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/blob/259a0e44e6b3c08c296ce12ba3509dd37fdc1ece/bbl/i18n/BambuStudio.pot#L2599)). After a cut, the slicer may also ask *Open edges may be caused by the cut tool, do you want to fix it now?*

## Bambu Studio says 1 non-manifold edge — is it safe to ignore?

Often yes: a single non-manifold edge far from any wall is usually closed by the slicer without a visible effect. Not if it sits on a wall or the sliced preview shows a missing region — then repair first, and run the [free check](/tools/repair-stl-online) to get the exact count and type so you decide with numbers.

To judge it yourself, slice the plate and scrub the layer preview around the flagged area: if every layer shows a closed outer wall, the edge did not matter.

---

## Why the Built-In "Repair" in Bambu Studio Often Fails

On Windows, Fix model hands the mesh to a repair service that ships with Windows — Bambu Studio's own progress message reads *Repairing object by Windows service*, and the [Bambu Lab wiki](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/software/bambu-studio/fix-model) describes the same Microsoft repair. It handles small defects, but it has three practical limits.

### 1. Painting and custom supports are removed
Before the Windows repair runs, Bambu Studio clears the model's painting: its own message says *Custom supports and color painting were removed before repairing* ([source](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/blob/259a0e44e6b3c08c296ce12ba3509dd37fdc1ece/bbl/i18n/BambuStudio.pot#L9228)). Repaint after the fix, or repair the STL first and paint afterwards.

### 2. It can hang or crash on complex files
Several public bug reports describe Fix model running for hours or closing Bambu Studio; the crash section below lists them and the workarounds.

### 3. Re-check critical dimensions
The repair can move vertices near the defect, so re-check critical dimensions after any automatic fix.

---

## Why is Fix Model missing or greyed out on Mac and Linux?

Bambu Studio's Fix model calls a repair API that Microsoft ships only with Windows — [Printing3DModel.RepairAsync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.printing3d.printing3dmodel.repairasync?view=winrt-28000), which "executes the 3D model repair algorithm on the model" — so on macOS and Linux the option is not offered at all rather than greyed out. In its place Bambu Studio shows the tip *To repair the model, please use a third-party tool before importing it into Bambu Studio*, which is what a Mac user reports in [BambuStudio issue #11174](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/11174) from June 2026.

The [Bambu Lab wiki's Fix Model page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/software/bambu-studio/fix-model) describes the same Windows-only repair. OrcaSlicer is the exception: since [OrcaSlicer PR #12155](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/pull/12155) (merged 24 Apr 2026, in the 2.4.0-alpha release notes of 25 May 2026) its Fix model uses CGAL and runs on Linux and macOS as well.

## Bambu Studio crashes when I click Repair — what to do

Public reports describe the same crash: [#12143](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/12143) (7 Sep 2026, version 2.8.2.61: "it keeps crashing when I click repair model"), [#11385](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/11385) (3 Jul 2026) and [#11288](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/11288) (25 Jun 2026). The ways out users report are going back to an earlier version — the reporter in [#12016](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/issues/12016) reinstalled 2.8.0.50, which worked — or repairing the file outside the slicer and re-importing it.

Repairing outside the slicer also tells you what was wrong: the free check lists every defect with its count before you spend anything.

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Inspect & Fix Non-Manifold Edges

### Method 1: Check and repair the file online, then re-import

1. Open **[Repair STL File Online](/tools/repair-stl-online)** and upload the STL, GLB or zipped OBJ (up to 200 MB). The check is free, runs on TEELI servers and needs no account.
2. Read the report: six checks — watertight, normals, duplicate vertices, degenerate triangles, self-intersections and scale — each with a pass, warning or fail and the count of every defect.
3. Repair costs 10 credits, and a new account starts with 25. If a repair fails or makes no progress, the credits are released; if it improves the file without reaching fully watertight, it is charged and the report says exactly what remained.
4. Download the repaired file and re-import it into Bambu Studio. Guest files and results are deleted 24 hours after upload.

Real engine results: on the holes.stl test file the health score went from 75 to 100 and the open holes from 1 to 0; on pinched_boundary.glb, geometry cut from a real customer asset, 36 open holes went to 0 with 0 non-manifold edges.

---

### Method 2: Manual Repair in Blender (Free Desktop Workflow)

If you prefer manual control inside desktop software:

1. Open Blender and import your broken `.stl` (`File > Import > Stl`).
2. Press `Tab` to enter **Edit Mode**.
3. Deselect all geometry by pressing `Alt + A`.
4. Go to top menu: `Select > Select All by Trait > Non Manifold` (or press `Shift + Ctrl + Alt + M`).
5. All non-manifold edges will highlight in bright orange.
6. To repair:
   - **Fill Holes:** Press `Alt + F` to fill open boundary loops with triangles.
   - **Recalculate Normals:** Press `A` to select all, then `Shift + N` to recalculate face normals outside.
   - **Merge Overlapping Vertices:** Press `M > By Distance` with a merge threshold of `0.001mm` to fuse unstitched seams.
7. Export as `.stl` (`File > Export > Stl`) and re-verify in your slicer.

---

## Slicer Geometry Repair Benchmark: Comparison Matrix

How do the repair options compare?

| Tool | Where it runs | Operating systems | Cost | What you get |

For a technical comparison of the file formats themselves, read **[STL vs OBJ vs 3MF for 3D Printing](/compare/stl-vs-obj-vs-3mf)**.

---

## Slicer Best Practices to Prevent Non-Manifold Errors

To avoid encountering non-manifold edge warnings in future projects:

- **Export as 3MF instead of STL:** Modern CAD systems (Fusion 360, SolidWorks, FreeCAD) export native `.3mf` files with proper topological connectivity data, eliminating the disconnected facet rounding errors common to legacy ASCII/Binary STLs.
- **Verify Boolean Union Operations:** When combining multiple shapes in CAD, ensure all parts are true Solid Bodies with non-zero wall thicknesses. Intersecting surface bodies with zero thickness will always generate non-manifold boundary seams.
- **Check Slicer Slicing Tolerance Settings:** In Bambu Studio (`Quality > Precision`), setting slicing tolerance to `Exclusive` rather than `Middle` can help avoid overlapping toolpaths on near-zero-clearance models.

---

## Summary & Next Steps

A non-manifold edge is a geometry problem, not a printer fault: the triangles do not enclose a closed solid. Check the count, decide with numbers, then repair inside the slicer on Windows or outside it on any OS.

faq.question: Why does Bambu Studio show 'Error: N non-manifold edges'?
faq.answer: Because some edges of the mesh are not shared by exactly two triangles — holes, internal walls or overlapping shells — so the slicer cannot tell inside from outside. Bambu Studio marks the object with a warning icon and offers Fix model on Windows.

faq.question: Can I ignore non-manifold edges and print anyway in Bambu Studio?
faq.answer: Often, if there are only a few and they sit away from any wall; check the sliced preview for missing regions first. Repair first if the edges sit on a wall, the count is large, or the part is functional.

faq.question: Does Bambu Studio repair non-manifold edges on Mac or Linux?
faq.answer: No. Fix model calls a repair API that Microsoft ships only with Windows, so on macOS and Linux Bambu Studio suggests a third-party tool instead. OrcaSlicer 2.4 and later has a CGAL-based Fix model that works on any OS.

faq.question: Why does the built-in repair remove my multi-color paint in Bambu Studio?
faq.answer: Bambu Studio clears custom supports and color painting before it runs the Windows repair, and its own message says so. Repaint after repairing, or repair the STL, which carries no paint, before you paint it.

faq.question: What is the easiest way to fix non-manifold edges on any OS?
faq.answer: Run the free check at teeli.net/tools/repair-stl-online to see every defect with its count, repair the file for 10 credits and re-import it into Bambu Studio. For full manual control, use the 3D-Print Toolbox in Blender instead.
